newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Former Guatemalan dictator denies 1980s massacres.
newsitem.headline: Former Guatemalan dictator denies 1980s massacres.

text.p: Former dictator General Efrain Rios Montt, the first Guatemalan leader called to account for huge state terror in the 1980s, on Tuesday denied any knowledge of massacres carried out under his regime.
Rios Montt was called as a witness in a government probe into the massacre of 350 civilians in a village in Guatemala's northern Peten jungle during the country's 36-year civil war.
"I neither ordered them, nor knew of them," he told reporters as he emerged from a private, two-hour interview with a state attorney conducting an inquiry into the killings.
Witnesses say the village of Dos Erres was wiped out in December 1982, months after Rios Montt took power in a coup.
Investigations began in 1994 with the exhumation of 166 cadavers, including 67 children under the age of 12, but so far no suspects have been named.

Among Guatemala's most controversial public figures, Rios Montt is championed by some as an honest, law-and-order leader and castigated by others as a brutal strongman who turned far-flung peasant villages into killing fields.
Guatemala's former Defence Minister and other top military officials are to testify in the case this week, public ministry attorney Mynor Melgar said.
